rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent-setting software (e.g., RealPage)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use rent-setting algorithms that rely on nonpublic competitor data, such as RealPage, to set rents. The source names no ordinance number and gives no effective date.
rules.key_value: Ban; reported fine of $2,000 per day
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Jersey City using rent-setting algorithm or revenue-management software that uses nonpublic data.
rules.exemptions: Reportedly excludes real estate agents. Owners of multiple buildings who use algorithms without colluding are reportedly not covered. Whether Multiple Listing Services are excluded was debated and is unresolved in the source.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the landlord uses algorithmic rent-setting software relying on nonpublic data.

rules.penalty: $2,000 daily fine (as characterized by a public commenter); private right of action suggested by an opponent's comments
rules.citation: Jersey City ordinance (number not stated in source)
rules.quoted_span: The Jersey City Council unanimously approved (9-0) a measure banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, as well as increasing benefits for laborers, at last night’s meeting.
rules.conflict_note: News article; no ordinance number, adoption date, or effective date given. Council members noted that amendments may still follow and raised enforceability concerns. The article also notes possible federal preemption: the House was considering barring municipalities from such actions. The in_force status is inferred from final passage.
